chunks: From him, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Munabbih ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān al-Kalabī, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:

I asked the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم about the junub and the menstruating woman who sweat in the garment until it clings to them. He said: Indeed, menstruation and janabah, where Allah Mighty and Majestic has placed them, are not from sweat; so they do not wash their garment.

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةَ: the state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: Does sweat from a junub person or a menstruating woman make clothing impure?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning sweat from a junub person and a menstruating woman when it affects a garment. It states that menstruation and janabah are situated where Allah عزّ وجلّ has placed them and are not derived from sweat, so the garment is not to be washed on that account.
